newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Profit downgrades mulled after DSM Q3.
newsitem.headline: Profit downgrades mulled after DSM Q3.

text.p: Analysts said on Tuesday they would likely reduce full-year earnings estimates for DSM after third-quarter profits at the Dutch chemicals group came in lower than expected.

Narrowing margins cut third-quarter operating profit to 239 million guilders from a year-earlier 342 million. Net profit came in at 178 million guilders compared with 234 million a year earlier, thanks to a lower tax bill and lower financial charges.
"Net profits were only slightly lower than the 186 million guilders we were expecting, but the quality of earnings has deteriorated," said Bert Schouten, analyst with MeesPierson.
"We had been more optimistic on operating profits," he said.
NIB Strating analyst Nils van Elzelingen agreed. "Obviously margins on hydrocarbons and polymers were even narrower than expected," he said.
Analysts said the situation was unlikely to improve in the fourth quarter.
"DSM said itself it will find it difficult to pass on higher feedstock prices," Van Elzelingen said.
Customers were purposely holding stocks low in anticipation of lower prices when new capacity came on stream in the fourth quarter, he said.
DSM itself was due to bring a new polypropylene plant on-stream some time in November, increasing its capacity from 350,000 to 500,000 tonnes, Van Elzelingen said.
"As a result capacity utilisation will come under pressure, leading to further price erosion," he predicted.
Schouten said the ongoing rise in the price of naphtha, the main feedstock for the plastics industry, could have a substantial impact on DSM's fourth quarter performance.
Higher naphtha prices coupled with an appreciating dollar meant DSM faces almost 30 percent higher costs than in the first quarter.
Both Schouten and Van Elzelingen said they would likely revise their 1996 earnings per share estimates downwards.
"I was looking at 25.90 guilders per share for 1996, I think this could be reduced slightly," Schouten said. Mees Pierson rates the stock as a Hold.
Van Elzelingen said he would be reducing his current profit per share estimates of 25.30 guilders for both 1996 and 1997.
"I'm looking to reduce both, with 1997 coming in lower than 1996," he said.
"My rating of DSM as an underperformer has only been strengthened by these results," Van Elzelingen said.
